approved.rationale: Direction consensus is unanimous short across all 4 perspectives. Technicals strongly favor the short side (both bears acknowledge it): daily ema_aligned_downtrend=true, price -10.45% below sma_50 and -16.41% below sma_200, adx_14=31.7 with minus_di 36.73 > plus_di 20.41, roc_21d=-14.49, and the 2026-05-28 -8% breakdown printed relative_volume=3.59 (8.67M vs avg 2.41M) through the 48.76 pivot support. The decisive disagreement is timing: both bears (bear_a 7, bear_b 6) argue the move is already extended/oversold (daily rsi_14=34.65, hourly rsi_21=29.32, bollinger pct_b=0.27, sitting on 11-tested support) so bounce risk is high; this exactly offsets the bull conviction (bull_a 7, bull_b 6), yielding combined_p_bull=0.50. Expected_return_per_share = 0.5*(48.40-44.50) - 0.5*(50.20-48.40) = 1.95 - 0.90 = +$1.05, positive, so the trade clears Gate 2 but on a thin edge (conviction held to 5). Position sizing: risk_dollars=$250 (1% x 1.0 scaling), risk_per_share=|48.40-50.20|=$1.80, Gate-3 quantity=floor(250/1.80)=138; notional 138x48.40=$6679 exceeds the 15% cap ($3750), so scaled down from 138 to 103 shares to fit small-account cap (103x48.40=$4985 <= 20% extended cap), using 74% of risk budget (risk_M=$185.40). Earnings 59 days out (no squeeze risk). Tight intraday window set given oversold bounce risk and a noise-wide ATR (atr_pct=6.85%).

Catalyst bull (b_bull_b.bull_strength=7) edges past the bears on R:R asymmetry, but the technical bears dominate on conviction (b_bear_a.bear_strength=8, b_bear_b.bear_strength=7 vs avg bull 6) and they are right on the facts: daily AND hourly rsi_divergence.bearish=true, daily rsi_7=85.42, bollinger pct_b=0.8945 pinned to upper band 1700.31, price +54.9% above sma_50, z_score_50=1.76, and the breakout printed on relative_volume=0.67 (below avg) - so this is an extended/exhaustion-prone entry, not a clean base break. Expected return is positive but thin: combined_p_bull=(0.3846+0.5)/2=0.4423; expected_return_per_share = 0.4423*(1770-1677.5) - 0.5577*(1677.5-1627) = 40.91 - 28.16 = +$12.75, carried entirely by the conservative target(min 1770)/stop(max 1627) asymmetry against a 55.8% bear-weighted probability. Sizing: risk_dollars=$250 (1% x 1.0), risk_per_share=$50.50, Gate-3 qty=floor(250/50.5)=4 -> notional $6,710 exceeds 15% cap ($3,750); scaled down from 4 to 2 shares to fit small-account cap, using 40% of risk budget (M=floor(5000/1677.5)=2, risk_M=$101 >= $100 floor). Conviction held to 4 given majority-bear probability, divergence flags, and below-avg breakout volume; entry kept as a tight day-order since a low-conviction extended breakout that doesn't fill fast is suspect.

Both bulls scored 4 while bear_a scored 6, so combined_p_bull=(4/(4+6)+4/(4+4))/2=0.45; expected_return_per_share=0.45*(208.50-202.875)-0.55*(202.875-198.40)=+$0.07, marginally positive so Gate 2 passes but conviction capped at 4. Key disagreement resolved in bears' favor on conviction: bear_a's thin-volume warning is supported by daily_indicators.volume.obv.trend='down'/diverging_from_price=true and relative_volume only 1.35, plus extension risk (bollinger.pct_b=1.1565, z_score_50=1.69, rsi_divergence.bearish=true) — but trend strength is real (adx_14=30.19, plus_di 24.83>>minus_di 6.57, price above all MAs), keeping EV positive. Sizing: risk_dollars=25000*1%=250, risk_per_share=|202.875-198.40|=4.475, Gate-3 qty=55 (notional $11,158 > 15% cap $3,750); scaled down from 55 to 24 shares to fit small-account cap, using 43% of risk budget (M=floor(5000/202.875)=24, risk_M=24*4.475=$107.40 >= 40%-floor $100).
